natural_body: 40% SMB discount: +31% signups, +18% rev, -12% ret; judge at renewal

first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down QoQ, and two independent inherited records (memory_31, memory_86) show durable gains from simplifying onboarding without noted retention cost, making it the safest lever directly addressing the current metric decline. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but its own record already flags a -12% retention effect judged only at renewal, so deploying it now under revenue-maximization risk is premature without re-verifying whether that retention hit held or reversed. I verify memory_73 to confirm whether the pricing risk is still current before ruling it out, and memory_31 to confirm the onboarding claim isn't stale or overlapping/duplicated with memory_86 before relying on both as corroboration. Choosing a standard_experiment (not broad_rollout) preserves the ability to observe downstream retention/revenue effects before committing further, and avoids locking into a discount-driven race-to-the-bottom against the competitor that could erode qualified revenue even if it recaptures signups.
